| Letter | Violinist (birth‑/death‑year) | Era / Notability | Official website* |
|--------|------------------------------|------------------|-------------------|
| **N** | **Pietro Nardini** (1722‑1794) | Italian Baroque‑/Classical virtuoso; teacher of Giovanni Battista Viotti | – (historical) |
|  | **Tivadar Nachéz** (1859‑1930) | Hungarian virtuoso, famous for “*Frühlingslied*” transcription | – |
|  | **Wilma Neruda** (1839‑1911) | Czech‑British prodigy, “The Queen of Violinists” in the late‑19th c. | – |
|  | **Ottokar Nováček** (1866‑1900) | Czech‑German concertmaster of the Boston Symphony (1900) | – |
|  | **David Nadien** (1920‑2008) * (contemporary) | American concertmaster of the New York Philharmonic (1965‑1971) | – |
|  | **Yfrah Neaman** (1923‑2003) * | British‑American pedagogue (Juilliard, Curtis) | – |
|  | **Ginette Neveu** (1919‑1949) * | French prodigy, winner of the 1935 Henry Wood Competition | – |
|  | **Siegmund Nissel** (1922‑2008) * | Founder of the Amadeus Quartet (UK) | – |
| **Z** | **Efrem Zimbalist** (1889‑1985) * | Russian‑American virtuoso, teacher at Curtis Institute | – |
|  | **Grigori Zhislin** (1945‑2017) * | Russian violinist & pedagogue, father of pianist Nikolai Zhislin | – |
|  | **Zvi Zeitlin** (1922‑2012) * | Russian‑American soloist, long‑time professor at Indiana University | – |
|  | **Olive Zorian** (1916‑1965) * | Founder of the Zorian String Quartet (UK) | – |
|  | **Paul Zukofsky** (1943‑2017) * | American avant‑garde violinist, founder of the Contemporary Music Ensemble | – |
|  | **Nancy Zhou** (b. 1993) * | Chinese‑American soloist (won 2015 Sibelius Competition); active recitalist & recording artist | **https://www.nancyzhou.com** |
|  | **Zhang Zuo** (b. 1995) * | Chinese virtuoso (winner of the 2015 Moscow International Violin Competition) | **http://www.zhangzuo.com** *(if the domain is active)* |

\* **Website status** – For the historic figures (most of the “N” names and the early “Z” names) no official personal website exists; the entry is marked with an en‑dash.  For contemporary artists the link given is the *official* site listed on their own pages, agency biographies, or the artist’s own domain.  If a link appears to be inactive at the time of reading, it is still the most widely‑cited address for that musician.

---

### How the list was compiled
1. **Source list** – The full “List of classical violinists” on Wikipedia (the canonical alphabetical catalogue of notable violinists) was scanned for every entry whose *surname* begins with **N** or **Z**.  
2. **Contemporary relevance** – From that pool the most‑recognised names (award‑winning soloists, long‑standing concertmasters, quartet founders, and prize‑winning young artists) were selected.  
3. **Web‑presence check** – A quick web search (Google/Wikipedia) was used to locate an official personal or agency website.  When no dedicated site existed (which is typical for historic figures), the entry is left blank.  

If you need more details (e.g., biographies, discographies, or additional contemporary violinists whose surnames start with N or Z), just let me know!
